meaning:
ἐχθρός, -ά, -όν
(ἔχθος, hatred), [in LXX chiefly for אֵיבָה, also for עָר, etc. ;]
1. hated, hateful (Hom.): opposite to ἀγαπητός, Rom.11:28.
2. Actively, hating, hostile: Rom.5:10, 1Co.15:25, 2Th.3:15; with genitive of person(s) (cl.), Jas.4:4; τ. διανοίᾳ, Col.1:21; ἐ. ἄνθρωπος, Mat.13:28; as subst., ὁ ἐ., an enemy, 1Co.15:26; the devil, Mat.13:39, Luk.10:19; with genitive of person(s), Mat.22:44 Mrk.12:36, Luk.20:43, Act.2:35, 1Co.15:25, Heb.1:13 10:13" (LXX) ; Mat.5:43-44 10:36 13:25, Luk.1:71, 74 6:27, 35 19:27, 43, Rom.12:20, Gal.4:16, Rev.11:5, 12; with genitive of thing(s), Act.13:10, Php.3:18.†
(AS)

elsewhere.note: “You have heard that it was said, ‘You shall love your neighbor and hate your enemy.’
For David himself said in the Holy Spirit, ‘The Lord said to my Lord, “Sit at my right hand, until I make your enemies the footstool of your feet.” ’
salvation from our enemies and from the hand of all who hate us;
until I make your enemies a footstool for your feet.” ’
For if while we were enemies, we were reconciled to God through the death of his Son, much more, being reconciled, we will be saved by his life.
For he must reign until he has put all his enemies under his feet.
